notes.heading: Radicals and their reactivity
points: A radical is a species with an unpaired electron; it is written with a dot, such as Cl• or •CH3.
Radicals are highly reactive because of the single unpaired electron.
Radicals form when a covalent bond splits so each atom keeps one of the two bonding electrons.

notes.heading: Homolytic fission makes radicals (initiation)
points: Homolytic fission: a covalent bond breaks with the shared pair split evenly, one electron to each atom, giving two radicals.
Halogens undergo homolytic fission when exposed to UV light or heat: Cl2 → 2Cl•.
This first step of a radical chain reaction is called initiation.
A single-barbed (fish hook) arrow shows one electron moving; a double-barbed arrow shows an electron pair moving.
In mechanisms, draw each arrow from where electrons start to exactly where they end.

notes.heading: Alkanes are unreactive; radical substitution
points: Alkanes are fairly inert: C–C (346 kJ mol⁻¹) and C–H (414 kJ mol⁻¹) bonds are strong and essentially non-polar.
Substitution replaces an atom or group in an organic molecule with another atom or group.
Alkanes react with halogens under UV light or heat by radical substitution: CH4 + Cl2 → CH3Cl + HCl.
Halogenation adds a polar C–halogen bond, making a more reactive molecule useful for further synthesis.

notes.heading: Propagation and termination steps
points: Propagation: a radical reacts with a non-radical, giving a new non-radical and a new radical, so the chain continues.
Step 1: CH4 + Cl• → •CH3 + HCl. Step 2: •CH3 + Cl2 → CH3Cl + Cl•.
Termination: two radicals combine to give a non-radical, lowering radical concentration and eventually stopping the reaction.
Termination examples: Cl• + Cl• → Cl2; •CH3 + Cl• → CH3Cl; •CH3 + •CH3 → C2H6.
The result is a mixture of products, including ethane as a by-product.

notes.heading: Which halogens work
points: Chlorine and bromine halogenate alkanes by radical substitution with UV light or heat.
Fluorine is too reactive and tends to break C–C bonds, giving a complex mixture.
Iodine is too unreactive, so radical iodination of alkanes does not occur.

definitions.definition: A molecular entity that has an unpaired electron, which makes it highly reactive.
definitions.trap: Do not say a radical is simply a charged species; it need not carry a charge.

definitions.definition: Breaking of a covalent bond so that each atom receives one of the two shared electrons, forming two radicals.
definitions.trap: Do not confuse with heterolytic fission, where one atom takes both electrons.

definitions.definition: The first step of a radical chain reaction, where homolytic fission of a halogen by UV light or heat produces radicals.
definitions.trap: Do not write UV light as a reactant; it supplies energy to break the bond.

definitions.definition: A step in which a radical reacts with a non-radical to form a new radical and a new non-radical, continuing the chain.
definitions.trap: Students write steps that use up two radicals; that is termination, not propagation.

definitions.definition: A step in which two radicals react to form a non-radical, reducing the number of radicals and ending the chain.
definitions.trap: Do not show a radical left over on the product side.

definitions.definition: Replacement of an atom or group of atoms in an organic molecule by another atom or group.
A single-barbed curly arrow showing the movement of one electron.
definitions.trap: A double-barbed arrow shows a pair of electrons, not one.
